turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi! How are you doing these days?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Why does my TV show black bars at the top and bottom on some films?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Those films are shot wider than your TV's shape. The bars keep the full picture without cutting off the sides.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I get rid of them?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can use the zoom setting on the TV, but it'll crop the edges of the image. The director framed it that way on purpose.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly, sometimes people at the edges of the frame just vanish. Most film fans keep the bars.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Huh. I always thought my TV was broken.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nope, it's doing its job. Some newer films even switch ratio for big scenes, so the bars come and go.
